grades.setting: Ask to Buy in Xbox Family Settings
grades.reason: Reviewers report children spent birthday money on Minecoins that did not arrive, were charged repeatedly for add-ons they never received, and found subscriptions presented as one-time payments. The help article notes enabling "Ask to Buy" in Xbox Family Settings sends an approval request each time a child tries to buy skins, texture packs, or Minecoins.

The App Store listing states the app uses tracking to deliver personalized ads and may use data to track users across other companies' apps and websites. A forum post adds that the developers share information with advertisers and directs readers to the privacy policy for details.

A rating description reports that if the game registers a player as under 13, purchases are locked, but it is very easy for a child to be aware of these restrictions and choose to enter a birth year that allows full access to all features.
Read the cited source quotes before deciding; we couldn’t verify a plain-language explanation for this area.

Another forum participant says any user can write text on signs their avatar holds up to communicate with everyone in the same game regardless of age.

Forum participants say Roblox encourages spending on Robux through limited-time events, exclusive items, and social pressure using freemium features.
